style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The psalm of fearless longing. It opens on the battlefield -- the LORD as light, salvation, and stronghold, so that armies can camp around David and his heart holds -- and then, in the middle of the war, it names the one thing: to dwell in the house of the LORD all his days, gazing on the LORD's beauty. The soldier's secret is that his fortress is a sanctuary; hidden in God's shelter, lifted onto the rock, he answers siege with singing. Then the weather changes at verse 7, as it does in real faith: the confident creed becomes an urgent plea -- hear me, do not hide Your face, do not cast me off -- grounded in the echo of God's own invitation, 'Seek My face.' Even the deepest human abandonment has a floor: when father and mother forsake, the LORD gathers him up. The psalm ends with David preaching to himself and to us the hardest discipline of the life of faith: wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait, I say, for the LORD.

1.text: Of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation -- whom should I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom should I be afraid?
1.amp: A Psalm of David. The LORD [YHWH] is my light [or] and my salvation [yesha]; whom shall I fear [yare]? the LORD is the strength [maoz -- the stronghold, the fortress] of my life [chay]; of whom shall I be afraid [pachad -- tremble in dread]?
1.notes: Three titles stacked against two fears: or (H216), light against every darkness; yesha (H3468), rescue against every threat; maoz (H4581), the fortress-height against every siege. yare (H3372) and pachad (H6342) are left as questions because, so guarded, they have no answer.

2.text: When evildoers came against me to devour my flesh, my adversaries and my enemies, it was they who stumbled and fell.
2.amp: When the wicked [raa], even my enemies [tsar] and my foes [oyeb], came ['approached against me', qarav, the KJV margin] upon me to eat up [akal] my flesh [basar], they stumbled [kashal] and fell [naphal].
2.notes: The enemies come as devourers, akal basar (H398, H1320), beasts closing on a carcass -- and the sentence ends with them on the ground: kashal and naphal (H3782, H5307). The confidence of verse 1 is not theory; David has watched this happen.

3.text: Though an army should encamp against me, my heart will not fear; though war itself should rise against me, even then I will keep trusting.
3.amp: Though an host [machaneh -- an army camp] should encamp [chanah] against me, my heart [leb] shall not fear [yare]: though war [milchamah] should rise [qum] against me, in this will I be confident [batach -- keep leaning my weight].
3.notes: The scenario escalates from raiders to a machaneh (H4264), a whole encamped army, to milchamah (H4421) itself standing up. batach (H982) is the leaning-trust of Psalm 22:4 -- 'in this', in the LORD of verse 1, the weight stays put.

4.text: One thing I have asked of the LORD, and that one thing I will keep seeking: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD, and to seek His counsel in His temple.
4.amp: One [echad] thing have I desired [shaal -- asked] of the LORD [YHWH], that will I seek [baqash] after; that I may dwell [yashab] in the house [bayith] of the LORD all the days [yom] of my life [chay], to behold [chazah -- gaze on, as a seer] the beauty ['the delight', noam, the KJV margin] of the LORD, and to enquire [baqar] in His temple [hekal].
4.notes: echad (H259): a life reduced to one request. chazah (H2372) is the seer's beholding, and noam (H5278) the LORD's delightfulness, His pleasantness -- the soldier's deepest want is not survival but the gaze. Mary chose this same 'one thing' at Jesus' feet (cf. Luke 10:42).

5.text: For in the day of trouble He will treasure me away in His shelter; in the hiding place of His tent He will conceal me; He will set me high upon a rock.
5.amp: For in the time [yom] of trouble [ra] He shall hide [tsaphan -- store up, treasure away] me in His pavilion [sok -- His shelter, His lair]: in the secret [sether -- the hiding place] of His tabernacle [ohel] shall He hide [satar] me; He shall set me up [rum -- lift me high] upon a rock [tsur].
5.notes: tsaphan (H6845) is to store as treasure: the hidden man is a hidden valuable. The sok (H5520) and the sether (H5643) of the ohel put David inside God's own tent -- sanctuary as stronghold -- and then rum (H7311) sets him on the tsur (H6697), high ground no siege reaches.

6.text: And now my head will be lifted high above the enemies who surround me, and in His tent I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing, yes, I will make music to the LORD.
6.amp: And now shall my head [rosh] be lifted up [rum] above my enemies [oyeb] round about me: therefore will I offer [zabach] in His tabernacle [ohel] sacrifices [zebach] of joy ['shouting', teruah, the KJV margin]; I will sing [shir], yea, I will sing praises [zamar -- make music] unto the LORD [YHWH].
6.notes: The same rum (H7311) that set him on the rock now lifts the rosh (H7218) above the encircling ring. teruah (H8643) is the battle-shout turned festal: the noise of war repurposed for worship, with shir (H7891) and zamar (H2167) -- voice and instrument -- both enlisted.

7.text: Hear my voice when I call, O LORD; be gracious to me, and answer me.
7.amp: Hear [shama], O LORD [YHWH], when I cry [qara] with my voice [qol]: have mercy [chanan -- be gracious] also upon me, and answer [anah] me.
7.notes: The psalm's hinge: the creed of verses 1-6 drops into present-tense need. chanan (H2603) asks for grace, not wages, and anah (H6030) for the answer -- the confident man still prays like a beggar, which is exactly why his confidence is real.

8.text: My heart repeats what You Yourself have said: 'Seek My face.' Your face, LORD, is what I will seek.
8.amp: When You said, 'Seek [baqash] ye My face [panim]'; my heart [leb] said [amar] unto You, 'Your face, LORD [YHWH], will I seek [baqash].'
8.notes: Prayer as echo: God's invitation baqash panim (H1245, H6440) goes out, and the leb answers it back word for word. All seeking of God begins as His seeking of us -- the heart merely returns the summons signed.

9.text: Do not hide Your face from me; do not turn Your servant aside in anger. You have always been my help; do not cast me off, do not forsake me, O God of my salvation.
9.amp: Hide [satar] not Your face [panim] far from me; put not Your servant [ebed] away [natah -- turn away] in anger [aph]: You have been my help [ezrah]; leave [natash] me not, neither forsake [azab] me, O God [Elohim] of my salvation [yesha].
9.notes: Five negatives in a row, prayed by the man told to seek the panim: losing that face is the only thing he cannot survive. azab (H5800) is the forsaking-word of Psalm 22:1 -- and 'God of my yesha' holds the title of verse 1 up as the argument.

10.text: Though my father and my mother forsake me, the LORD will gather me up.
10.amp: When my father [ab] and my mother [em] forsake [azab] me, then the LORD [YHWH] will take me up ['gather me', asaph, the KJV margin].
10.notes: The deepest human bond named and released: even ab and em can azab. asaph (H622) is to gather in -- the word for taking a foundling off the street into one's own house. The floor under every abandonment is adoption (cf. Isaiah 49:15).

11.text: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path, because of those who lie in wait for me.
11.amp: Teach [yarah] me Your way [derek], O LORD [YHWH], and lead [nachah] me in a plain ['a way of plainness', mishor, the KJV margin] path [orach], because of my enemies ['those which observe me', shorer, the KJV margin].
11.notes: yarah (H3384) is to teach as an archer aims. The mishor (H4334) is level ground, no stumbling stones -- needed because the shorer, the watchers, wait for exactly one misstep. Holiness of walk is also tactical wisdom under hostile eyes.

12.text: Do not hand me over to the appetite of my adversaries, for false witnesses have risen against me, breathing out violence.
12.amp: Deliver [natan -- give] me not over unto the will [nephesh -- the appetite, the soul] of my enemies [tsar]: for false [sheqer] witnesses [ed] are risen up [qum] against me, and such as breathe out [yapheach] cruelty [chamas -- violence].
12.notes: The enemies' nephesh (H5315) here is raw appetite -- do not feed me to it. sheqer ed (H8267, H5707) is perjury, the courtroom weapon, and chamas (H2555) the violence it licenses. The Messiah stood before exactly such witnesses (cf. Matthew 26:59-60).

13.text: Unless I had believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living -- I would have fainted away.
13.amp: I had fainted, unless [lule] I had believed [aman -- held firm, trusted] to see [raah] the goodness [tuv] of the LORD [YHWH] in the land [eretz] of the living [chay].
13.notes: The Hebrew breaks off mid-sentence -- 'unless I had believed... ' -- and the unstated collapse speaks louder than words; the KJV supplies 'I had fainted'. aman (H539) is faith as holding firm, and the hope is concrete: God's tuv (H2898) seen here, in the eretz of the living, not only beyond it.

14.text: Wait for the LORD. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Wait, I say, for the LORD.
14.amp: Wait [qavah -- wait with hope, as for a rope to pull taut] on the LORD [YHWH]: be of good courage [chazaq -- be strong], and He shall strengthen [amats] your heart [leb]: wait, I say, on the LORD.
14.notes: qavah (H6960), from the word for a cord: waiting as tension held toward God, not slack resignation. chazaq (H2388) is the command and amats (H553) the gift -- be strong, and He strengthens. The doubled 'wait' is David preaching to his own leb, the same sermon every waiting believer must repeat.
